newsitem.title: UK: LME copper jittery after borrowers stand back.
newsitem.headline: LME copper jittery after borrowers stand back.

text.p: LME copper ended Monday morning nervous and wounded when spreads flared only briefly then fizzled out, wrong-footing many players.
Most of the other metals followed copper off their highs, but aluminium was robust, hovering near its highs.
Three months copper lost contact with the key $2,400 a tonne level, spiralling into the negative column after an expected frenzy of covering on nearby dates failed to materialise, traders said.
"I have to admit, I was surprised," said a floor trader.
"It looks like the market got itself a bit long...it doesn't look very comfortable," another said.
Traders had been awaiting Monday's trading because the first tight date of a string, April 30, became prompt. Shorts suffering from a squeeze were expected to be forced to cover at high rates.
In the first ring, the scenario began as expected when the cash/day spread zipped up to a $16 backwardation, a wide spread, but under the $26 limit imposed by the LME.
Things soon came unglued, however, when borrowing dried up and the spreads lost steam. The cash/day narrowed to a $8 backwardation by the end of the first ring, ending the morning at $5/$10.
After the first bout of covering, borrowers stood back as spreads were offered lower and lower.
By the end of morning kerb, the benchmark cash/threes spread had slumped to a $125/130 backwardation after trading at $210 earlier in the morning and cash/May narrowed to $40/$45 from about $110.
There was still potential for more tightness in coming days, however, with some traders believing that shorts stepped back temporarily and will still be forced to jump back in and cover.
Three months finished the morning with a $6 loss at $2,377 after earlier moving as high as $2,407.
Support was expected at $2,360/65 and stops expected below $2,350. On the upside stops were believed to lurk around $2,415, traders said.
Aluminium streaked higher, peaking at $1,641 resistance in the morning and maintaining a positive spirit in the face of copper's slide. It finished the morning an impressive $21 higher at $1,634.
The threes/average 1998 spread flipped into backwardation as widespread forward selling entered the market, traders said.
It was bid up to an $11 backwardation compared to a $17/$20 contango on Friday. If three months achieves the $1,650 mark, the spread could see a $50 backwardation, one floor trader said.
At one point the cash/threes spread narrowed to a $23 backwardation from $27/$26 on Friday, but heavy lending by a major European trade house pulled it back out to Friday's level.
On Friday, borrowing of the early July to the July date tightened the market, bringing the cash/threes in from a more normal $32 the previous day.
Most of the other metals followed copper's lead, exploring higher, but finishing softer.
Zinc touched $1,280 but ended the morning down $5 at $1,270, while nickel achieved $7,540 before easing back to $7,450, a $30 loss.
Lead gained $4 to $635 in sluggish activity while tin was quiet, last indicated at $5,710,30, down from $5,740.
Alloy climbed with the primary market, adding $15 to $1,505/10.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom ++44 171 542-8065
